newsitem.title: USA: American's pilots board approves labor contract.
newsitem.headline: American's pilots board approves labor contract.

text.p: The board of American Airlines' pilots union voted Friday to approve a labor contract proposed by the nation's second-largest air carrier, union officials said.

The five-year agreement includes a 9 percent wage increase, a stock option program and a guarantee that furloughed pilots will be tapped to fly new jets the carrier is buying for its American Eagle regional airline.
The board of the Allied Pilots Association, which represents 9,300 American Airlines pilots, voted by a margin of 12 to six, union officials told a news conference.
Rank-and-file members of the union are expected to vote on the contract within two months, APA President James Sovich told reporters.
The 18-member board met all day Thursday to discuss the proposed contract, but recessed without a vote.
The issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, was the focus of the meetings on Thursday.
American Airlines pilots are concerned they might lose routes to American Eagle if American buys new smaller jets for the regional subsidiary.
American Airlines is a subsidiary of AMR Corp.
